­vegetables and fruits on a daily basis. This recommendation should emphasize inclu-
sion of dark green, leafy, and deep yellow vegetables as well as colorful fruits. Sweets 
and desserts should be offered only occasionally, instead offering nutrient-dense food 
for dessert such as fruit, cheese, yogurt, and cereals. Beverages should consist of 
water, limited amounts of 100% fruit juice, and low-fat milk for children over 2 years 
of age. The practice of offering toddlers several snacks daily was commonly observed. 
Because toddlers received about 25% of their calories from snacks, the importance of 
providing planned nutrient-rich foods at snack-time becomes apparent. Five servings 
(serving = 1 tablespoon/year of age) of fruit and vegetables daily as well as three 
­servings of dairy foods should remain a goal for toddlers.42
